statement: (i) Show that $\\frac{d}{dx}(x\\ln x-x)=\\ln x$. (ii) Using integration by parts, evaluate $\\int_{1}^{e}(\\ln x)^{2}\\,dx$ and show it equals $e-2$.
solution: (i) $\\frac{d}{dx}(x\\ln x-x)=\\ln x+1-1=\\ln x$. (ii) Let $u=(\\ln x)^{2}, dv=dx$; then $\\int(\\ln x)^{2}dx=x(\\ln x)^{2}-2\\int\\ln x\\,dx=x(\\ln x)^{2}-2(x\\ln x-x)$. From $1$ to $e$: at $e$, $e-2e+2e=e$; minus at $1$: $0-0+2=2$. So value $=e-2$.
hints: Integrate $(\\ln x)^{2}$ by parts, reusing part (i).
